The full size image must be fetched from the host site on hover so yes your IP is part of the request sent to the host. Once it is showing on your browser, the image is in your browser cache and therefore on your machine. Hover zoom is not magic and it doesn't protect you one bit. Interesting why do others claims that so and so app is better than the other then? Why was there security concerns with hover zoom and not the others?

They all have the same security concerns. In order for an image to show on your screen, a request has to be sent somewhere. While the app/plugin might act as a proxy for you and shield your IP from the image host, the app's host still got your IP. It has to in order to send the image to you. The concern is that the app host now has (potential) logs of your visit and what you requested. It could also be an outright honeypot gathering IPs and logging content requests. You just can't be fully safe since there is a long tail in every internet resource request. And, once the image is displayed on your computer, it is there no matter what the app you used is. The only way to make this completely independent on storage issues is to have the image data loaded exclusively into RAM and flushed immediately after you are done viewing it. Browsers don't work that way. You would need something custom made to prevent the image data from hitting your disk. There's just no fully secure way to avoid the issues except for not using the internet or a computer, but then you can't see any online images.
